messages:
Priya: quick async check — hitting a contract weirdness w/ stop + max_tokens + logprobs when streaming. Observed: if stop sequence fires the stream ends and `logprobs` field is often missing for the trailing token. Is that expected or a bug?

Alex: Hmm, we should get logprobs for the last emitted token even if stop triggered. Can you paste a minimal repro?

Priya: yea, repro below (hosted API):
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-1\",
  \"prompt\": \"List colors:\n1. Red\n2. Blue\n3. \",
  \"max_tokens\": 16,
  \"stop\": [\"\\n4.\"],
  \"temperature\": 0.2,
  \"top_p\": 0.95,
  \"logprobs\": 5,
  \"stream\": true
}
```
Observed stream ends when it emits the stop and then the final JSON chunk has no `logprobs` key (or `tokens` array). On previous contract we had `tokens` + `logprobs` even for stop-triggered termination.

Joanna: could be streaming truncation codepath: we drop per-token metadata for the stop chunk when we synthesize an early-terminate event. If this is a regression we should fix. Is this across Hosted/Dedicated/Private?

Priya: repro on Hosted and Dedicated canary. Private not tested.

Sam: two angles: 1) backward-compatibility — callers assume logprobs always present when requested. 2) implementation — some runtimes treat stop as zero-length emission (synthetic) so no token-level stats. I think we should preserve logprobs for the last real token, and if we emit a synthetic stop marker, add an explicit `termination_reason` field instead of dropping `logprobs`.

Alex: agree. Proposal: API contract rule — when `logprobs` is requested, the final emitted token(s) before termination must include `logprobs` and `tokens` arrays. If termination is due to stop sequence, include an extra field `stop_sequence: string|null` in the final event. That keeps it backward compatible (callers still get token stats).

Joanna: opt-in change? or must for all versions? Breaking change if we change stream chunk shapes. I'd prefer to make this a patch: always include the arrays but keep them empty only if genuinely no token emitted. Also document streaming event shapes in API docs.

Priya: sounds good. Quick checklist: 
- PR in runtime to carry per-token metadata through stop synthesis (Alex)
- API docs update + example (Joanna)
- Add a small integration test that requests `logprobs` + `stop` + `stream` and asserts final chunk contains `logprobs` (Sam)
- Canary deploy on Dedicated then Hosted (Priya)

Sam: I'll add the integration test and a unit test for the streaming serializer. Ping me on the PR.

Alex: started a draft branch: refs/heads/fix/stream-logprobs-stop — pushing in a bit.

infra-bot: deploy check queued for branch fix/stream-logprobs-stop — will run canary in dedicated-qa (ETA ~25m).

Priya: awesome. Last question: any nuance with temp/top_p interplay? I asked because one caller saw different tokenization when temp=0 vs temp>0 and thought stop matching changed.

Joanna: deterministic sampling (temp=0) shouldn't change stop matching behavior; token sequence is deterministic though sampling can alter emitted tokens which influences where a stop can match. We should note this in docs: stop sequences match on emitted token stream, so sampling affects whether a stop occurs but not the matching algorithm.

Priya: perfect. Will wait for the canary and tests. Thanks everyone :pray:
